findings.title: getSubGroupsCount returns null for a vanished group, breaking the never-null contract and hiding the missing group
findings.description:
The new line 275, `return model == null ? null : model.getSubGroupsCount();`, returns null when `modelSupplier.get()` is null. That happens when the group row no longer exists and the adapter has not been invalidated, so `isUpdated()` (lines 70-76) returns false. `GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount()` is documented as "Never returns null" (server-spi/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/GroupModel.java:296). The same missing-row condition elsewhere in this class throws `IllegalStateException("Not found in database")` (GroupAdapter.java:61 and 74).

The path is: `GroupsResource.getGroups` (GroupsResource.java:113 or 124) → `GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount` (GroupUtils.java:90) → `setSubGroupCount(null)`. The deleted group is returned to the client with a null count instead of being excluded or failing. Before this change the same path threw an NPE. I searched the Java sources, and no caller unboxes the value, so the impact is the contract violation and the null in the response, not a crash. A fix should either throw like the sibling methods or drop the vanished group from the listing. If null is intended, the interface Javadoc has to change.

findings.title: Assertion runs without joining the reader thread, so late exceptions are never checked
findings.description: The reader thread started at lines 139-149 is never joined. `deletedAll.set(true)` at line 155 only signals the loop to stop. A `groups(...)` call already in flight keeps running, and any exception it throws is added to `caughtExceptions` after `assertThat` at line 157 has already read the list. The test can pass while a concurrent read failed, which is the condition it exists to catch. Keep a reference to the thread and `join()` it before asserting.

findings.title: A failing remove() leaves the polling reader thread running indefinitely
findings.description: `deletedAll.set(true)` at line 155 runs only if every `remove()` call in the loop at line 153 returns normally. If one throws, for example on a non-2xx response, the exception leaves the test before the flag is set. The reader thread at lines 139-149 then loops with no sleep and no stop condition. It is non-daemon and never joined, so it keeps sending brief-listing requests to the shared server for the rest of the test JVM's life. Set the flag in a `finally` block, and make the thread a daemon or join it.
